correctness.rationale: PASS. The regular tetrahedron uses vertices (+/-1,+/-1,+/-1) of even parity, so its edge length is 2 sqrt(2); viewing normals are Haar-uniform on S2. Its projected area is A(u)=2 max(sum_i |u_i|, 2 max_i |u_i|) and the shadow is triangular exactly when sum_i |u_i|>2 max_i |u_i|, with spherical measure-zero boundaries excluded. The eight triangular and six quadrilateral spherical cells have cap and cap/hemisphere intersection areas. The stated segment function G_h(t)=2[acos(h/sqrt(1-t^2))-t acos(ht/sqrt((1-h^2)(1-t^2)))] yields the type-weighted sub-CDFs, correct transition radii 2sqrt2, 4sqrt(2/3), 2sqrt3, 4, constant upper density on each type and common leading lower-tail coefficient 3/(2sqrt2*pi). Independent 1,200,000-Haar-direction simulation agreed at eleven cutoffs with both exact formulas; these checks corroborate but do not replace the spherical-area proof. Prior unconditional area density and type-conditional moments recover as consequences; no distribution for asymmetric tetrahedra is claimed.
residual_risks: Applies only to Haar-uniform orthogonal projections of the stated regular tetrahedron scale; no arbitrary tetrahedron or perspective claim.

Independent numerical sampling is corroboration only; exact universality rests on spherical integral proof.

originality.rationale: PASS after direct primary comparisons. Vickers and Brown (2001) derive the regular tetrahedron marginal projected-area PDF and discuss triangles/quadrilaterals, but §3(ii) and Appendix B report unconditioned density, not two separately labeled type CDFs. A previously published SCOPE paper gives the exact first two conditional moments for arbitrary tetrahedra, including this regular case, but explicitly not the full conditional area distribution. These prior results and their obvious tail implications are credited; the complete two subdistribution functions, internal transitions and common quadratic onset are not entailed by just the marginal and low moments. The classical geometric method is related and priority remains historically uncertain.
